History & Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
27-year-old woman with 2-day history of constant dull lower-abdominal ache associated with nausea and subjective fever; mild urinary frequency and recent light vaginal spotting; requires same-day face-to-face GP assessment to rule out pregnancy, urinary or pelvic pathology.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant dull ache below the umbilicus for the last 2 days, accompanied by nausea and feeling hot/sweaty.  
• Onset/progression: Gradual onset 2 days ago; symptoms persistent and described as “getting uncomfortable.”  
• Associated urinary symptoms: Increased frequency of micturition; no dysuria, no urgency, no foul odor; urine noted to look slightly pink over the last couple of days.  
• Gastrointestinal: No vomiting; prior constipation one week ago now resolved; normal bowel movement yesterday; no diarrhoea.  
• Gynaecologic: Last menstrual period ≈3–3½ weeks ago; expecting period soon. Mild spotting over last few days. Sexually active with one regular partner. Uses etonogestrel implant (Implanon). Unsure but thinks pregnancy unlikely. No vaginal discharge, no dyspareunia reported.  
• Constitutional: Subjective fever (hot/sweaty). Denies light-headedness or fainting.  
• Review of other systems: No shoulder-tip pain, no syncope; other systems not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Drug allergy: Amoxicillin.  
• No other drug allergies noted.  
• Medications: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
• Lives with boyfriend.  
• Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol and recreational drug use not discussed.  
• Occupation/financial factors not discussed.

Family History:
• Brother with type 1 diabetes.  
• No other familial illnesses recalled.

Physical Examination:
• No in-person examination performed during tele-consult.  
• Vitals not obtained.

Investigations:
• None to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute lower-abdominal pain with nausea, spotting, urinary frequency  
  Assessment: Differential includes urinary tract infection, early intra-uterine or ectopic pregnancy, pelvic inflammatory disease, early appendicitis, and less likely residual constipation (supported by DDx).  
  Plan:  
  • Arrange same-day face-to-face GP appointment for abdominal and pelvic examination.  
  • Point-of-care or laboratory urine pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy/ectopic.  
  • Urinalysis ± urine culture to assess for UTI.  
  • Consider pelvic swabs if PID suspected after examination.  
  • Provide safety-net advice: seek urgent care if pain escalates, develops light-headedness, new bleeding, vomiting, or other concerning symptoms.

Issue 2 – Subjective fever  
  Assessment: Likely secondary to underlying urinary or pelvic pathology.  
  Plan:  
  • Temperature measurement at in-person review.  
  • Further investigations (e.g., CBC, CRP) per GP clinical judgment.

Issue 3 – Medication/Allergy review  
  Assessment: Amoxicillin allergy documented.  
  Plan:  
  • Ensure alternative antibiotics are selected if infection confirmed.  
  • No regular oral medications to reconcile.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Urinary tract infection (cystitis ± early pyelonephritis) – Likelihood: High  
   • Fits urinary frequency, suprapubic ache, subjective fever, nausea; absence of dysuria does not exclude.  
2. Early pregnancy or ectopic pregnancy – Likelihood: Moderate  
   • Pelvic pain, light spotting, nausea; highly effective contraception lowers but does not abolish risk.  
3. Pelvic inflammatory disease – Likelihood: Moderate  
   • Lower-abdominal pain, systemic symptoms, spotting; no discharge but still possible.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vital signs, physical exam findings, current medication list beyond implant; alcohol history not obtained; detailed allergies beyond amoxicillin not confirmed.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear, occasional minor pauses but all clinically relevant data intelligible.
